aspect_assessments.assessment: The response data support composition-dependent sensing, but support for a reducing-gas shift is endpoint-dependent. n-GaN-20 responded more strongly to NO2 and had the lowest directly measured TMA limit at 1 ppm, compared with 5 ppm for InGaN-20 and 10 ppm for InGaN-15. Calculated TMA LODs reverse that ranking, with InGaN-20 lowest at 8.94 ppb, followed by InGaN-15 at 34.4 ppb and n-GaN-20 at 143.9 ppb. The packet therefore supports different response profiles within tested gases, not uniform superiority of In-containing sensors for reducing gases.
limitations: Directly measured limits and calculated LODs produce different TMA rankings and must be assessed separately.
Figure pixels and replicate uncertainty were not inspected.

add_nodes.statement: In vitro, the ordered BTen and trabecular-like BT architectures direct TDSCs and BMSCs differently when pore size, porosity and material are held similar.
The printed BTen and BT scaffolds reproduce their intended architectures with measured pore size, porosity and Ti6Al4V composition similar between them.
BTen supports TDSC adhesion, alignment and proliferation more than BT, whereas BT supports BMSC adhesion and proliferation more than BTen.
BTen promotes tenogenic differentiation of TDSCs relative to BT (tendon markers at protein and mRNA level), beyond any difference in cell number.
BT promotes osteogenic differentiation and mineralization of BMSCs relative to BTen, beyond any difference in cell number.
In the rabbit model, the BR prosthesis achieves more coordinated bone-prosthesis and tendon-prosthesis integration than BTen or BT prostheses.
A trabecular-like prosthesis body (BT, BR) gives more bone ingrowth and bone-prosthesis integration than an ordered body (BTen) at 6 and 12 weeks.
An ordered top cap (BTen, BR) gives more soft tissue coverage and tenogenic tissue at the tendon-prosthesis interface than a trabecular-like cap (BT).
The tendon-prosthesis interface of BR withstands a higher load to failure than those of BTen and BT.
Within BR, tissue phenotype is partitioned by region: tenogenic, fibrous tissue at the top cap and osteogenic, bone-like tissue in the body.

proposed_updates.rationale: One root per setting; child aspects map to requirements r01 (a02-a05), r02 (a07), r03 (a08, a09) and r04 (a10).

findings.description: After SIE, OLE did not modify the PDH rise (o14) but increased OXPHOS and MitoCarta gene sets at Post and 24 h (o20, o22), so the visible SIE data do not show the PDH step that n13 places upstream of the transcriptional response.

PDH activity is only a proxy for Ca2+ uptake (n27). A saturated readout is possible given the SIE main time effect (o13), but that effect is pooled over OLE and PLA and the Pre vs Post comparison gave P = 0.055 after excluding one PLA participant, so a ceiling is a possibility to test rather than a demonstrated fact; the PDH null therefore does not exclude a Ca2+ effect.

At Post, OLE increased OXPHOS gene expression after SIE (o20) while having no detectable effect on inflammatory pathways (o18); inflammatory attenuation and mTOR/UPR suppression with OLE appear only at 24 h, so an inflammation-based route can address the 24 h response only.
The OLE-associated rise in mitochondrial transcripts after SIE coexists with a further OLE-associated decrease of mitochondrial proteins (o26) and no western blot change (o24).

add_nodes.statement: OLE may raise mitochondrial and OXPHOS gene expression after SIE through a route that does not require additional mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake or PDH activation. For the 24 h response, one candidate instance is dampening of the exercise-induced inflammatory and proteostasis stress response (inflammatory, mTOR and unfolded protein response pathways attenuated at 24 h), relieving SIE-induced suppression of mitochondrial transcription; this instance does not explain the Post increase, when no OLE effect on inflammatory pathways was detected. Unverified proposal.

proposed_updates.rationale: Offers a Ca2+/PDH-independent account of the SIE transcript response, consistent with the unchanged PDH rise; the inflammatory instance is scoped to 24 h because o18 shows no OLE inflammatory effect at Post while o20 shows the OXPHOS increase already at Post. Kept as a competing, unverified explanation beside n13.

findings.description: Grade labels and chemistry come from manufacturer declarations and literature, so the chemistry link needs sample-level measurements before it can be tested.
Product-level consistency across days is exposed to drift, which the constraints state was not evaluated.

information_requests: How many sessions and calendar days the repeated runs of each product span.

add_nodes.statement: Run-level grade discrimination: classifiers given the five-channel BME688 record of a run assign held-out runs to high, medium or low grade above the three-class chance level, with all runs of a product held out together during cross-validation.

Channel contribution: grade discrimination obtained from the gas-resistance and IAQ channels is compared with that from the temperature, humidity and pressure channels alone, to establish which signals carry the grade information.

Pipeline comparison: a raw-waveform deep model and PCA-reduced summary-statistic classical classifiers are compared on the same runs under one identical product-grouped cross-validation protocol with comparable, test-fold-independent tuning.
Per-class comparison: per-class F1 of both pipelines, with attention to the medium grade whose indicative polyphenol and ORAC ranges lie between the other two grades.
Proposed mechanism (unverified): the temporal shape of the heated VOC-release trace (rise, peak, decay, plateau) carries grade information beyond per-channel summary statistics.

Product-level consistency: for each product, the fraction of its repeated runs assigned to the dominant predicted class and whether that class matches the assigned grade, computed from predictions made with the product held out.
Retest stability: grade verdicts for the same product remain stable across measurement sessions on different days, including under slow sensor baseline drift.

Chemical correspondence: sensor-trace features covary with measured headspace composition (for example GC-MS terpene alcohols versus short-chain aldehydes) and with measured polyphenol, ORAC and caffeine values of the same samples.
Label and product confounds: discrimination is not explained by product form (loose, bag, cup bag) or added flavoring (bergamot) that co-occur with grade in the 16-product set.

proposed_updates.rationale: One or more separately testable aspects per requirement; the release-shape mechanism is marked as a proposal linking the comparison and chemistry aspects; confound and channel aspects make the run-level claim interpretable.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Three-class chance level and the same protocol for all models
missing_design_information: How tuning or early stopping is kept independent of the test fold
needed_observations: F1-macro and per-class F1 for every model under the same product-grouped cross-validation
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Do both pipelines discriminate grade when all runs of each product are held out together?
verification_needs.why_informative: Separates product-independent grade information from product-identity cues shared by repeated runs.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Same products measured at different dates with baseline re-referencing
missing_design_information: Number of sessions and days per product
needed_observations: Per-product dominant class and consistency rate
Repeat measurements of the same products weeks apart
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Are product verdicts stable across repeated sessions and over time?
verification_needs.why_informative: Shows whether screening verdicts survive retesting and drift.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Correlation of sensor features with measured compound levels across products
needed_observations: GC-MS headspace profiles and polyphenol/ORAC/caffeine assays of the measured samples
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Do trace features track sample-level aroma chemistry?
verification_needs.why_informative: Tests the chemistry link instead of inferring it from label-level grades.

needed_observations: Channel-restricted model performance

findings.description: The root claim bundles material, single-unit and module-level performance; each needs its own test and comparator.
CO testing is capped at 50 ppm (k01), so CO calibration, selectivity and mixture tests are bounded by that ceiling.

add_nodes.statement: The PVDF-HFP/NaTFSI/TPFPB/PC i-TE polymer combines a large-magnitude ionic thermopower S with a low thermal conductivity kappa (high S/kappa), and its thermopower changes little across relative humidity.
A single microfabricated sensing unit (carbon-black absorber on an i-TE pillar) converts incident infrared power into voltage with high responsivity (V/W).
A single sensing unit responds to and recovers from an infrared on/off step on a time scale compatible with gas monitoring.
Each gas channel's output decreases monotonically with its target-gas concentration in N2 and follows the modified Beer-Lambert relation, giving a calibration curve over the tested range.
Each gas channel's response to its target gas is unchanged by the presence of the other target gases (no cross-sensitivity between the CO2, CO and CH4 channels).
Concentrations estimated from the channel outputs with the per-channel calibration curves agree with the set concentrations of CO2/CO/CH4 mixtures across the tested range.
The 3900 nm reference-channel output tracks emitter intensity and optical-path attenuation independently of gas composition, so it can correct drift in the gas channels.
Channel outputs are repeatable across repeated exposures and stable over long operation (hours to weeks).
Relative humidity does not materially change the packaged unit's output or the gas readings obtained with humidified gas streams.
Limits of detection computed from calibration noise and slope (3 sigma_y/sigma) reach the ppm-to-ppb range for each gas.

Filtered infrared light absorbed by the carbon-black layer creates a temperature gradient across the i-TE polymer, and unequal cation/anion thermodiffusion (Soret effect) produces the voltage; target gases reduce this voltage by absorbing at their characteristic wavelengths.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each requirement is split into aspects that need separate evidence: material S/kappa and humidity (a01), unit responsivity (a02) and timing (a03), per-channel calibration (a04), cross-gas selectivity (a05), mixture quantification (a06), reference-channel drift correction (a07), stability over time (a08), humidity robustness (a09) and LOD (a10). The b08 photothermal/Soret mechanism (a11) links the material to the channel responses.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The public analyses support a modest donor-level increase in whole-lung NUFIP1 in IPF, with a significant Wilcoxon comparison and a concordant but non-significant pseudobulk sensitivity result; one continuous pathway association with MYC targets V1 survives correction while the other seven prespecified signatures and all 27 marker genes do not; no discrete NUFIP1-defined subgroup or clinical association is supported; and NUFIP1 is detected across lineages rather than being fibroblast-specific. These are five separate statements resting on five separate analyses.

No survival, longitudinal FVC decline, glutamate, protein-interaction or treatment-response measurements in these datasets

aspect_assessments.rationale: The comparator here is saline instillation, which addresses induction under injury rather than the consequence of raising NUFIP1.
aspect_assessments.scope: Male C57BL/6 mice, single intratracheal bleomycin dose of 5 mg/kg, day-21 endpoint.

findings.description: The donor-level Wilcoxon comparison and the donor-pseudobulk DESeq2 analysis test the same contrast in the same donors but under different aggregation and inference procedures, and they give different verdicts (P = 0.011 versus FDR = 0.330). The second is the robustness check that bounds how strongly the first can be read, so both are required.

Within the same public data, the correlation analysis tests continuous covariation with prespecified pathway scores and marker genes, the mixture-model analysis tests whether donors fall into a NUFIP1-defined subgroup with clinical correlates, and the single-cell analysis tests where NUFIP1 is expressed across lineages and fibroblast states. Different analysis units and separate multiple-testing families make them non-interchangeable.

Both mouse studies report hydroxyproline, histology, micro-CT and Vimentin, but one compares bleomycin with saline to test whether NUFIP1 is induced during fibrosis, and the other compares AAV-NUFIP1 with AAV-vector to test whether raising NUFIP1 produces fibrosis; the bleomycin arm of the three-group design is also the reference for the comparable-magnitude statement.

No visible analysis connects the experimental gain-of-function readouts to the public cohorts, because those datasets contain no NUFIP1 protein, complex-formation, glutamate or treatment-response measurements.

answer.no_change_reason: No two visible records cover the same requirement. The two bulk analyses of the same donors differ in aggregation and inference and disagree in outcome, so the second is the robustness check for the first rather than a copy of it. The correlation analysis, the mixture-model and clinical-association analysis, and the single-cell lineage analysis test three different statements with different analysis units and separate multiple-testing families. The two mouse studies share readouts but differ in manipulation and comparator, bleomycin against saline versus AAV-NUFIP1 against AAV-vector, and the bleomycin arm additionally serves as the reference group for the comparable-magnitude statement. Merging any of these pairs would discard a distinct requirement or a provenance that the current interpretations depend on, so all plans, observations and links are kept as they are.

findings.description: Requirement rq03 has no map aspect, and no visible observation addresses repeated use of the catalyst.

add_nodes.statement: Stability: CNCM(1:1) retains its coupled H2 evolution and TC removal activity, and its structure, over repeated runs under the coupled test conditions.

Activity retention: the H2 evolution rate and TC removal efficiency of CNCM(1:1) do not decline appreciably over several consecutive coupled runs (for example five) with a stated TC replenishment protocol.
Material integrity: used CNCM(1:1) keeps the crystal and chemical structure of both PCN and MVCM, the Ce3+/Ce4+ state of MVCM, and its Pt cocatalyst, without appreciable Ce leaching.

proposed_updates.rationale: rq03 requires stability, and the map has no aspect for it. The added aspect separates activity retention from material integrity, because the partially oxidized Ce-MOF phase and the in situ deposited Pt are specific stability risks.

verification_needs.why_informative: This shows whether the activity reported for a single run is sustained, which the stability requirement asks for.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Partly supported. All coatings slowed weight loss and softening relative to uncoated fruit, and PPMP-A1.5 did so most. The permeability premise holds for oxygen relative to neat PPMP but not for water vapor, and the between-blend OP differences are small. The coating effect on respiration was non-significant.
limitations: Coating thickness on fruit is measured only for PPMP-A1.5.
Between-blend OP significance not stated.
aspect_assessments.rationale: The size of the fruit-outcome differences does not track the size of the material-permeability differences.
aspect_assessments.scope: Free-film permeability measured on 86-126 µm cast films; fruit outcomes at 25 °C and 64% RH over 8 days.

findings.description: The statement that PPMP-A1.5 has the lowest water permeability conflicts with o08, in which WVP of the blends is comparable and higher than that of neat PPMP.

add_nodes.statement: Candidate alternative (unverified): the better outcomes of PPMP-A1.5-coated fruit relative to PPMP-A0.5 and PPMP-A1 arise mainly because more coating is deposited and retained on the peel. The higher-solids PPMP-A1.5 solution may leave a thicker or more continuous layer after three dips, and PPMP-A1.5 is the most water-resistant material, so its layer may persist better on the moist fruit surface. Differences in the intrinsic oxygen or water vapor permeability of the materials would then play a smaller role, since WVP is comparable and OP differs little among the three blends.

proposed_updates.rationale: The ordering of fruit outcomes follows coating thickness and water resistance at least as closely as it follows the similar permeabilities of the blends. The alternative competes with n19 and remains a proposal.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: PPMP-A0.5 and PPMP-A1 coatings adjusted (dip number or solids) to match the PPMP-A1.5 deposit, compared with standard application
missing_design_information: Fruit per group per time point
needed_observations: Coating thickness from SEM cross-sections and dry-mass pickup per fruit for PPMP-A0.5, PPMP-A1 and PPMP-A1.5
Coating continuity on the peel over storage at 64% RH
Weight loss, firmness and CO2 for coatings applied at matched deposited dry mass
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Is the formulation ordering of fruit outcomes explained by the amount of coating on the fruit rather than by material permeability?
verification_needs.why_informative: If the ordering disappears at matched deposit, the alternative is favored; if it persists, intrinsic material properties (n19) are favored.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Both halves of the sufficiency aspect have matching evidence at the scope claimed. In culture, NUFIP1 overexpression raised Vimentin relative to the negative control vector under the conditions of that panel. In vivo, AAV-NUFIP1 produced histological and micro-CT remodeling with higher hydroxyproline and Vimentin than AAV-vector controls, and the magnitude was described as comparable to the separate bleomycin arm. The interpretations restate these contrasts without widening them. The aspect statement itself names the TGF-beta1 stimulation background of the culture comparison and the AAV-vector comparator in vivo, so it does not reach beyond either design.
limitations: Vimentin is the only activation readout visible for the culture panel and for lung protein levels
Comparability with the bleomycin arm is qualitative; no equivalence test is reported
No visible observation lowers endogenous NUFIP1, so necessity is untested
MRC-5 is a fetal line and does not reproduce adult or IPF fibroblast features

add_nodes.statement: Effect of OLE vs PLA on the vastus lateralis mitochondrial bioenergetic response to one exercise session, judged separately within the MICE group and within the SIE group
OLE vs PLA changes vastus lateralis PDH activity from Pre to Post MICE (within-participant crossover)
OLE vs PLA further increases the Pre-to-Post rise in vastus lateralis PDH activity induced by SIE (within-participant crossover)

OLE vs PLA modifies mitochondrial-related gene expression (oxidative phosphorylation and other mitochondrial gene sets) at Post and 24 h, relative to the exercise response with PLA, within each exercise group
OLE vs PLA modifies mitochondrial protein levels (individual OXPHOS complex subunits and the mitochondrial proteome) at Post and 24 h, within each exercise group
Effect of OLE vs PLA on performance-related responses during the session
OLE vs PLA changes mean HR during fixed-workload MICE (1 h at 50% MAP), i.e. cardiovascular load at the same external power

add_nodes.statement: Hypothesis to be tested: hexaprotonated meso-tetra(pyridyl)porphyrins anchored to nanoAmbSO3H or nanoAmbSO3Na are leaching-stable, oxidatively stable and active heterogeneous photosensitizers.
The anchored porphyrins are present as hexaprotonated species (Soret and Q-band shifts relative to the free bases, matching the dissolved hexaprotonated salts).
The porphyrins occupy the polymer mesopores (changes in surface area, pore volume and pore-size distribution relative to the bare support).
Porphyrin incorporation changes the polymer's thermal behaviour relative to the bare supports.
Nanocomposite particle size and dispersibility in water.
No detectable release of porphyrin into water or organic solvents during long exposure, in dark and under light.
Photocatalytic activity of the composites versus dissolved hexaprotonated and free-base porphyrins, judged separately for BG, RhB and methyl phenyl sulfide.
Oxidative degradation of immobilized versus dissolved porphyrins under the same reaction conditions.
Oxidative degradation of immobilized porphyrins under extended irradiation, with and without substrate.
Identity of the reactive oxygen species for each catalyst type and substrate (scavenger tests).
Singlet oxygen quantum yield of each photosensitizer measured against a standard in the same solvent.
Retention of activity over successive reuse runs.
Effect of support form (nanoAmbSO3Na versus nanoAmbSO3H) on singlet oxygen quantum yield and activity at matched loading.
Higher dye-oxidation yields with hexaprotonated porphyrins may partly reflect acid-accelerated dye oxidation rather than better photosensitization.
Support-form differences in activity may reflect substrate adsorption on the support rather than singlet oxygen generation.

findings.description: n01 combines a manipulation premise (RDN lowers sympathetic activity), two outcome domains (LV function; scar and fibrosis) and a macrophage question; the objective adds an in vitro beta-adrenergic question. These need separate aspects with their own comparisons.

information_requests: Whether the design includes an RDN plus sham-ligation group to show RDN effects without MI.

add_nodes.statement: RDN reduces renal sympathetic activity in the treated rats: renal NE content and renal TH protein are lower in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats at study end, with CTRL showing whether MI itself raises these markers.

RDN attenuates the post-MI decline in LV systolic function: LVEF by cardiac MRI 4 weeks after ligation is higher in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats, with CTRL defining the MI-induced decline; myocardial BNP expression serves as a supporting marker.

RDN reduces chronic scar size and fibrotic remodeling: scar area on collagen-stained LV sections and fibrogenic markers (collagen I, TGF-beta, CTGF mRNA/protein) at 4 weeks are lower in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats.

RDN changes cardiac macrophage abundance and phenotype after MI: a pan-macrophage marker (CD68), the reparative/profibrotic marker CD206 (mRNA, protein, cell counts) and proinflammatory markers (CXCL10, CD80) differ between RDN+MI and sham-RDN MI rats.
Myocardial CD206 expression co-varies with the extent of fibrosis across animals (an association).

Beta-adrenergic stimulation shifts macrophage gene expression toward a profibrotic, less proinflammatory profile in vitro: isoprenaline versus vehicle in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells, with beta1-selective (CGP 20712A) and beta2-selective (ICI 118,551) antagonists identifying the receptor subtype.
RDN does not impair kidney function or change systemic laboratory values (plasma creatinine, urea, electrolytes, glucose, liver enzymes), so cardiac differences are not secondary to renal injury.
Proposed and unverified: lower sympathetic drive after RDN limits beta1-adrenergic induction of a profibrotic, CD206-high macrophage phenotype, which reduces fibrosis and preserves LV function.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each aspect maps to one separately measurable comparison. p01 is the manipulation check the SNS attribution depends on; p02 and p03 separate function from structure; p04-p06 separate in vivo marker changes, their association with fibrosis, and the in vitro receptor test; p07 addresses a renal confound; p08 keeps the causal chain as a proposal.

add_nodes.statement: PCN/MVCM (CNCM) heterojunctions give efficient concurrent visible-light H2 evolution and TC degradation, with TC as the only sacrificial agent, above PCN and MVCM alone.
Composite formation: CNCM contains both PCN and MVCM phases in intimate contact (electron microscopy with EDS, XRD, FTIR, porosimetry).
H2 evolution: CNCM evolves H2 faster than PCN and MVCM under the coupled conditions, with a composition optimum across the Ce-MOF:PCN ratios.
TC removal: CNCM degrades more TC than PCN and MVCM under the same conditions, distinguished from adsorption by dark controls and from partial transformation by TOC or product analysis.
Stability: the optimized composite keeps H2 and TC activity and its structure over repeated coupled runs.
Reactive species: the species (h+, •O2−, •OH, e−) driving TC degradation, and separately their effect on H2 evolution, under the coupled conditions.
Charge separation: the heterojunction reduces recombination and improves charge transport relative to PCN and MVCM (PL, impedance, photocurrent).
Band alignment: the relative CB and VB positions of PCN and MVCM form a staggered alignment in which PCN electrons can reduce H+ and MVCM holes can oxidize TC.
Transfer direction: the direction of interfacial electron transfer in the dark (contact) and under illumination (photogenerated carriers) across the PCN/MVCM interface.
Coupling: TC oxidation (including intermediates) enhances H2 evolution by consuming holes, and H2 evolution does not impair TC degradation, tested against matched single-reaction conditions.
Degradation pathway: the intermediates and routes of TC transformation and the extent of mineralization.

Proposed S-scheme mechanism (unverified): an internal field from PCN to MVCM drives recombination of MVCM CB electrons with PCN VB holes, leaving PCN CB electrons for H+ reduction and MVCM VB holes for TC oxidation.
Competing explanation (unverified): type-II transfer, in which photogenerated electrons move to the MVCM conduction band and holes to the PCN valence band.

proposed_updates.rationale: One aspect per requirement, with H2 and TC as separate endpoints and the transfer direction separated from static band alignment, because the S-scheme and its type-II competitor share the same alignment.

findings.description: a08 combines band alignment, dark contact charge transfer and the photoinduced transfer direction, which require separate evidence.

information_requests: State the electrolyte, pH and frequency used for the Mott-Schottky measurements.

add_nodes.statement: Band alignment: PCN has more negative conduction- and valence-band edges than MVCM (staggered alignment), from Mott-Schottky flat-band potentials, the 0.1 eV offset and Tauc gaps. This is compatible with either a type-II or an S-scheme pathway.

Contact charge transfer in the dark: in CNCM(1:1), electrons move from PCN to MVCM before illumination. PCN-derived C 1s and N 1s binding energies rise and MVCM-derived lattice O 1s and Ce 3d binding energies fall relative to the pristine components, which implies an interfacial field from PCN to MVCM.

Photoinduced transfer direction: under illumination, photogenerated electrons move from MVCM to PCN (the XPS shifts reverse), as expected if MVCM conduction-band electrons recombine with PCN valence-band holes (S-scheme) rather than accumulate in MVCM (type-II).

Retained redox capability: after transfer, electrons remain at the PCN conduction band for H+ reduction and holes at the MVCM valence band for TC oxidation. This requires evidence locating the reduction and oxidation sites.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each sub-aspect has its own evidential basis: static energetics (o13, o17, o18), dark XPS shifts (o19, dark), light XPS shifts (o19, light), and reaction-site evidence that this view does not contain. m01 remains the proposed mechanism linking them.

verification_needs.why_informative: The two pathways predict different reduction and oxidation sites. This gives evidence on the transfer direction that does not depend on XPS binding-energy interpretation.

aspect_assessments.assessment: An association between NUFIP1 and ZNHIT3 is supported: ZNHIT3 co-precipitates with NUFIP1 from fibroblast lysates and binds immobilized NUFIP1 in a cell-free assay with a dissociation constant of 5.26 x 10^-7 M. Recovered immunoprecipitated NUFIP1 differed among conditions
The two systems used different CB-839 concentrations, 10 micromolar cell-free versus 0.5 micromolar in culture
No quantitative ZNHIT3 comparison between IPF and control tissue is reported

aspect_assessments.assessment: The glutamate-supply mechanism is consistent with the cellular data but is not distinguished from explanations acting directly on the proteins. CB-839 lowers glutamate and raises glutamine in NUFIP1-overexpressing fibroblasts, and the association readouts fall under treatment; however, the affinity change was measured with purified components where no glutaminase step exists, so at least part of the effect cannot be attributed to reduced glutamine-derived glutamate. Steady-state pool sizes, not fluxes, were measured, and no experiment adds glutamate back or perturbs glutaminase genetically.
limitations: No glutamate or alpha-ketoglutarate add-back and no genetic glutaminase perturbation
Glutamine and glutamate were measured as steady-state pools without flux measurements
CB-839 inhibits glutaminase and can affect other glutamine-dependent processes
aspect_assessments.rationale: A mechanism that requires enzymatic conversion in cells cannot act in a cell-free binding run, so the affinity result is evidence about the compound and the proteins rather than about glutamate supply.
aspect_assessments.scope: MRC-5 fibroblasts with ectopic NUFIP1 for the metabolite and co-precipitation readouts; purified proteins for the affinity readout.

findings.description: The measured drop in apparent affinity occurred in a purified-protein system where glutaminase activity and glutamine-to-glutamate conversion are absent, and the same design states that CB-839 was passed over the immobilized NUFIP1. A direct interaction of CB-839 with NUFIP1, competing with or allosterically weakening ZNHIT3 binding, therefore explains that observation without invoking glutamate supply.

The cellular co-immunoprecipitation cannot separate a change in bound fraction from a change in recovered bait or in partner abundance, because recovered immunoprecipitated NUFIP1 differed among conditions and no input-normalised quantification is shown.

add_nodes.statement: CB-839 interacts directly with NUFIP1 and weakens ZNHIT3 binding by competition or by an allosteric change at the binding surface, so the reduced apparent affinity and reduced co-precipitation reflect a compound-protein interaction rather than lower glutamine-derived glutamate. Within BR, tissue phenotype is partitioned by region: tenogenic, fibrous tissue at the top cap and osteogenic, bone-like tissue in the body.

findings.description: After SIE, OLE did not modify the PDH rise (o14) but increased OXPHOS and MitoCarta gene sets at Post and 24 h (o20, o22), so the visible SIE data do not show the PDH step that n13 places upstream of the transcriptional response.

PDH activity is only a proxy for Ca2+ uptake (n27). A saturated readout is possible given the SIE main time effect (o13), but that effect is pooled over OLE and PLA and the Pre vs Post comparison gave P = 0.055 after excluding one PLA participant, so a ceiling is a possibility to test rather than a demonstrated fact; the PDH null therefore does not exclude a Ca2+ effect.

At Post, OLE increased OXPHOS gene expression after SIE (o20) while having no detectable effect on inflammatory pathways (o18); inflammatory attenuation and mTOR/UPR suppression with OLE appear only at 24 h, so an inflammation-based route can address the 24 h response only.
The OLE-associated rise in mitochondrial transcripts after SIE coexists with a further OLE-associated decrease of mitochondrial proteins (o26) and no western blot change (o24).

add_nodes.statement: OLE may raise mitochondrial and OXPHOS gene expression after SIE through a route that does not require additional mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake or PDH activation. For the 24 h response, one candidate instance is dampening of the exercise-induced inflammatory and proteostasis stress response (inflammatory, mTOR and unfolded protein response pathways attenuated at 24 h), relieving SIE-induced suppression of mitochondrial transcription; this instance does not explain the Post increase, when no OLE effect on inflammatory pathways was detected. Unverified proposal.

proposed_updates.rationale: Offers a Ca2+/PDH-independent account of the SIE transcript response, consistent with the unchanged PDH rise; the inflammatory instance is scoped to 24 h because o18 shows no OLE inflammatory effect at Post while o20 shows the OXPHOS increase already at Post. findings.description: Grade labels and chemistry come from manufacturer declarations and literature, so the chemistry link needs sample-level measurements before it can be tested.

add_nodes.statement: Run-level grade discrimination: classifiers given the five-channel BME688 record of a run assign held-out runs to high, medium or low grade above the three-class chance level.

Channel contribution: grade discrimination obtained from the gas-resistance and IAQ channels is compared with that from the temperature, humidity and pressure channels alone, to establish which signals carry the grade information.
Pipeline comparison: a raw-waveform deep model and PCA-reduced summary-statistic classical classifiers are compared on the same runs with comparable, test-fold-independent tuning.
Per-class comparison: per-class F1 of both pipelines, with attention to the medium grade whose indicative polyphenol and ORAC ranges lie between the other two grades.
Proposed mechanism (unverified): the temporal shape of the heated VOC-release trace (rise, peak, decay, plateau) carries grade information beyond per-channel summary statistics.

Product-level consistency: for each product, the fraction of its repeated runs assigned to the dominant predicted class and whether that class matches the assigned grade, computed from predictions made with the product held out.
Retest stability: grade verdicts for the same product remain stable across measurement sessions on different days, including under slow sensor baseline drift.

Chemical correspondence: sensor-trace features covary with measured headspace composition (for example GC-MS terpene alcohols versus short-chain aldehydes) and with measured polyphenol, ORAC and caffeine values of the same samples.
Label and product confounds: discrimination is not explained by product form (loose, bag, cup bag) or added flavoring (bergamot) that co-occur with grade in the 16-product set.

proposed_updates.rationale: One or more separately testable aspects per requirement; the release-shape mechanism is marked as a proposal linking the comparison and chemistry aspects; confound and channel aspects make the run-level claim interpretable.

add_nodes.statement: The PVDF-HFP/NaTFSI/TPFPB/PC i-TE polymer combines a large-magnitude ionic thermopower S with a low thermal conductivity kappa (high S/kappa), and its thermopower changes little across relative humidity.
A single microfabricated sensing unit (carbon-black absorber on an i-TE pillar) converts incident infrared power into voltage with high responsivity (V/W).
A single sensing unit responds to and recovers from an infrared on/off step on a time scale compatible with gas monitoring.
Each gas channel's output decreases monotonically with its target-gas concentration in N2 and follows the modified Beer-Lambert relation, giving a calibration curve over the tested range.
Concentrations estimated from the channel outputs with the per-channel calibration curves agree with the set concentrations of CO2/CO/CH4 mixtures across the tested range.
The 3900 nm reference-channel output tracks emitter intensity and optical-path attenuation independently of gas composition, so it can correct drift in the gas channels.
Channel outputs are repeatable across repeated exposures and stable over long operation (hours to weeks).
Relative humidity does not materially change the packaged unit's output or the gas readings obtained with humidified gas streams.
Limits of detection computed from calibration noise and slope (3 sigma_y/sigma) reach the ppm-to-ppb range for each gas.

Filtered infrared light absorbed by the carbon-black layer creates a temperature gradient across the i-TE polymer, and unequal cation/anion thermodiffusion (Soret effect) produces the voltage; target gases reduce this voltage by absorbing at their characteristic wavelengths.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each requirement is split into aspects that need separate evidence: material S/kappa and humidity (a01), unit responsivity (a02) and timing (a03), per-channel calibration (a04), mixture quantification (a06), reference-channel drift correction (a07), stability over time (a08), humidity robustness (a09) and LOD (a10). The b08 photothermal/Soret mechanism (a11) links the material to the channel responses.

findings.description: The donor-level Wilcoxon comparison and the donor-pseudobulk DESeq2 analysis test the same contrast in the same donors but under different aggregation and inference procedures, and they give different verdicts (P = 0.011 versus FDR = 0.330). The second is the robustness check that bounds how strongly the first can be read, so both are required.

Within the same public data, the correlation analysis tests continuous covariation with prespecified pathway scores and marker genes, the mixture-model analysis tests whether donors fall into a NUFIP1-defined subgroup with clinical correlates, and the single-cell analysis tests where NUFIP1 is expressed across lineages and fibroblast states. Different analysis units and separate multiple-testing families make them non-interchangeable.

Both mouse studies report hydroxyproline, histology, micro-CT and Vimentin, but one compares bleomycin with saline to test whether NUFIP1 is induced during fibrosis, and the other compares AAV-NUFIP1 with AAV-vector to test whether raising NUFIP1 produces fibrosis; the bleomycin arm of the three-group design is also the reference for the comparable-magnitude statement.

No visible analysis connects the experimental gain-of-function readouts to the public cohorts, because those datasets contain no NUFIP1 protein, complex-formation, glutamate or treatment-response measurements.

information_requests: The number of donors contributing to each fibroblast state in the single-cell summaries, so that pooled-cell percentages can be read at the sample level
Replicate numbers and effect sizes for the mouse hydroxyproline and western blot readouts in both models
answer.no_change_reason: No two visible records cover the same requirement. The two bulk analyses of the same donors differ in aggregation and inference and disagree in outcome, so the second is the robustness check for the first rather than a copy of it. The correlation analysis, the mixture-model and clinical-association analysis, and the single-cell lineage analysis test three different statements with different analysis units and separate multiple-testing families. The two mouse studies share readouts but differ in manipulation and comparator, bleomycin against saline versus AAV-NUFIP1 against AAV-vector, and the bleomycin arm additionally serves as the reference group for the comparable-magnitude statement. Merging the correlation and mixture-model records and omitting their separate provenance would simplify the answer.

findings.description: Free-base porphyrins must be tested in acetonitrile, so activity comparisons with water-tested forms change solvent as well as protonation.

add_nodes.statement: Hypothesis to be tested: hexaprotonated meso-tetra(pyridyl)porphyrins anchored to nanoAmbSO3H or nanoAmbSO3Na are leaching-stable, oxidatively stable and active heterogeneous photosensitizers.
The anchored porphyrins are present as hexaprotonated species (Soret and Q-band shifts relative to the free bases, matching the dissolved hexaprotonated salts).
The porphyrins occupy the polymer mesopores (changes in surface area, pore volume and pore-size distribution relative to the bare support).
Porphyrin incorporation changes the polymer's thermal behaviour relative to the bare supports.
Nanocomposite particle size and dispersibility in water.
No detectable release of porphyrin into water or organic solvents during long exposure, in dark and under light.
Photocatalytic activity of the composites versus dissolved hexaprotonated and free-base porphyrins, judged separately for BG, RhB and methyl phenyl sulfide.
Oxidative degradation of immobilized versus dissolved porphyrins under the same reaction conditions.
Oxidative degradation of immobilized porphyrins under extended irradiation, with and without substrate.
Identity of the reactive oxygen species for each catalyst type and substrate (scavenger tests).
Singlet oxygen quantum yield of each photosensitizer measured against a standard in the same solvent.
Retention of activity over successive reuse runs.
Effect of support form (nanoAmbSO3Na versus nanoAmbSO3H) on singlet oxygen quantum yield and activity.
Higher dye-oxidation yields with hexaprotonated porphyrins may partly reflect acid-accelerated dye oxidation rather than better photosensitization.
Support-form differences in activity may reflect substrate adsorption on the support rather than singlet oxygen generation.

add_nodes.statement: RDN reduces renal sympathetic activity in the treated rats: renal NE content and renal TH protein are lower in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats at study end, with CTRL showing whether MI itself raises these markers.

RDN attenuates the post-MI decline in LV systolic function: LVEF by cardiac MRI 4 weeks after ligation is higher in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats, with CTRL defining the MI-induced decline; myocardial BNP expression serves as a supporting marker.

RDN reduces chronic scar size and fibrotic remodeling: scar area on collagen-stained LV sections and fibrogenic markers (collagen I, TGF-beta, CTGF mRNA/protein) at 4 weeks are lower in RDN+MI than in sham-RDN MI rats.

RDN changes cardiac macrophage abundance and phenotype after MI: a pan-macrophage marker (CD68), the reparative/profibrotic marker CD206 (mRNA, protein, cell counts) and proinflammatory markers (CXCL10, CD80) differ between RDN+MI and sham-RDN MI rats.
Myocardial CD206 expression co-varies with the extent of fibrosis across animals (an association).

Beta-adrenergic stimulation shifts macrophage gene expression toward a profibrotic, less proinflammatory profile in vitro: isoprenaline versus vehicle in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells, with beta1-selective (CGP 20712A) and beta2-selective (ICI 118,551) antagonists identifying the receptor subtype.
RDN does not impair kidney function or change systemic laboratory values (plasma creatinine, urea, electrolytes, glucose, liver enzymes), so cardiac differences are not secondary to renal injury.
Lower sympathetic drive after RDN limits beta1-adrenergic induction of a profibrotic, CD206-high macrophage phenotype, which reduces fibrosis and preserves LV function.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each aspect maps to one separately measurable comparison. p01 is the manipulation check the SNS attribution depends on; p02 and p03 separate function from structure; p04-p06 separate in vivo marker changes, their association with fibrosis, and the in vitro receptor test; p07 addresses a renal confound; p08 keeps the causal chain as a proposal.

add_nodes.statement: PCN/MVCM (CNCM) heterojunctions give efficient concurrent visible-light H2 evolution and TC degradation, with TC as the only sacrificial agent, above PCN and MVCM alone.
Composite formation: CNCM contains both PCN and MVCM phases in intimate contact (electron microscopy with EDS, XRD, FTIR, porosimetry).
H2 evolution: CNCM evolves H2 faster than PCN and MVCM under the coupled conditions, with a composition optimum across the Ce-MOF:PCN ratios.
TC removal: CNCM degrades more TC than PCN and MVCM under the same conditions, distinguished from adsorption by dark controls and from partial transformation by TOC or product analysis.
Stability: the optimized composite keeps H2 and TC activity and its structure over repeated coupled runs.
Reactive species: the species (h+, •O2−, •OH, e−) driving TC degradation, and separately their effect on H2 evolution, under the coupled conditions.
Charge separation: the heterojunction reduces recombination and improves charge transport relative to PCN and MVCM (PL, impedance, photocurrent).
Band alignment: the relative CB and VB positions of PCN and MVCM form a staggered alignment in which PCN electrons can reduce H+ and MVCM holes can oxidize TC.
Transfer direction: the direction of interfacial electron transfer in the dark (contact) and under illumination (photogenerated carriers) across the PCN/MVCM interface.
Coupling: TC oxidation (including intermediates) enhances H2 evolution by consuming holes, and H2 evolution does not impair TC degradation, tested against matched single-reaction conditions.
Degradation pathway: the intermediates and routes of TC transformation and the extent of mineralization.

Proposed S-scheme mechanism (unverified): an internal field from PCN to MVCM drives recombination of MVCM CB electrons with PCN VB holes, leaving PCN CB electrons for H+ reduction and MVCM VB holes for TC oxidation.
Competing explanation (unverified): type-II transfer, in which photogenerated electrons move to the MVCM conduction band and holes to the PCN valence band.

proposed_updates.rationale: One aspect per requirement, with H2 and TC as separate endpoints and the transfer direction separated from static band alignment, because the S-scheme and its type-II competitor share the same alignment.

add_nodes.statement: Band alignment: PCN has more negative conduction- and valence-band edges than MVCM (staggered alignment), from Mott-Schottky flat-band potentials, the 0.1 eV offset and Tauc gaps. This is compatible with either a type-II or an S-scheme pathway.

Contact charge transfer in the dark: in CNCM(1:1), electrons move from PCN to MVCM before illumination. PCN-derived C 1s and N 1s binding energies rise and MVCM-derived lattice O 1s and Ce 3d binding energies fall relative to the pristine components, which implies an interfacial field from PCN to MVCM.

Proposed photoinduced transfer direction: under illumination, photogenerated electrons may move from MVCM to PCN (the XPS shifts reverse), as expected if MVCM conduction-band electrons recombine with PCN valence-band holes (S-scheme) rather than accumulate in MVCM (type-II). This remains a proposed mechanism to be tested.

Proposed retained redox capability: under the S-scheme hypothesis, electrons would remain at the PCN conduction band for H+ reduction and holes at the MVCM valence band for TC oxidation. This requires evidence locating the reduction and oxidation sites.

proposed_updates.rationale: Each sub-aspect has its own evidential basis: static energetics (o13, o17, o18), dark XPS shifts (o19, dark), light XPS shifts (o19, light), and reaction-site evidence that this view does not contain. m01 remains the proposed mechanism linking them.

Vehicle composition and matching across the cell-free binding conditions, and the number of replicate runs per condition

add_nodes.statement: CB-839 interacts directly with NUFIP1 and weakens ZNHIT3 binding by competition or by an allosteric change at the binding surface, so the reduced apparent affinity and reduced co-precipitation reflect a compound-protein interaction rather than lower glutamine-derived glutamate. This is a candidate explanation, not an observed result.

The cellular change in co-precipitated ZNHIT3 under CB-839 reflects differences in recovered immunoprecipitated NUFIP1 or in cellular ZNHIT3 and NUFIP1 abundance rather than a change in the bound fraction of the complex. This is a candidate explanation, not an observed result.

proposed_updates.rationale: The affinity shift was obtained with purified components, where the proposed metabolic step cannot occur, and the cellular readout has unequal recovered bait. Both facts are visible in the packet, and each supports a specific competing account that should sit beside the glutamate mechanism rather than replacing it.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: CB-839 as analyte versus vehicle-only injections over the same immobilized NUFIP1 surface, with an unrelated immobilized protein as a specificity control
missing_design_information: Vehicle and its concentration in the reported CB-839 runs
Whether the reported CB-839 injections over immobilized NUFIP1 produced a response and what parameters were obtained
Number of replicate runs per condition and the fitting model applied to the reported rate constants
needed_observations: Surface plasmon resonance with CB-839 alone as analyte over immobilized NUFIP1 across a concentration series that brackets 10 micromolar, with buffer and vehicle-matched controls
Replicate ZNHIT3 binding runs at matched vehicle concentration, before treatment, during CB-839 exposure and after washout
The same ZNHIT3 titration in the presence of glutamate or alpha-ketoglutarate added to the running buffer
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Does CB-839 bind NUFIP1 directly at concentrations that reduce apparent ZNHIT3 affinity?
verification_needs.why_informative: Measurable direct binding of CB-839 to NUFIP1 near the concentration used would explain the affinity shift without glutamate, while the absence of direct binding, together with reversal on washout, would weaken that alternative. Adding glutamate to a system with no glutaminase separates a glutamate requirement of the complex itself from a requirement for glutamine conversion.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Genetic glutaminase perturbation versus non-targeting control, each with and without glutamate add-back, at matched NUFIP1 expression and input ZNHIT3
missing_design_information: Achievable glutaminase knockdown level tolerated by these fibroblasts
Input and bait quantification for the reported co-immunoprecipitation
Whether CB-839 alters cellular ZNHIT3 or NUFIP1 abundance
needed_observations: Co-immunoprecipitation of ZNHIT3 with NUFIP1 in fibroblasts after GLS knockdown or knockout versus non-targeting control, quantified relative to recovered immunoprecipitated NUFIP1 and with input blots for both proteins
The same readout with glutamate or alpha-ketoglutarate add-back, and with a glutaminase inhibitor of a different chemical class at a matched exposure
Intracellular glutamate measured in the same samples
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Does reducing glutaminase activity genetically, rather than pharmacologically, weaken the cellular NUFIP1-ZNHIT3 association, and is any such change reversed by supplying glutamate?
verification_needs.why_informative: A genetic perturbation removes compound-specific off-target actions, add-back tests whether glutamate is the limiting intermediate, and bait-normalised quantification removes the recovery artefact that currently limits the cellular result.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Interface variants versus wild-type proteins under identical assay conditions
missing_design_information: Whether recombinant variant proteins are available and fold correctly
Expression level matching between variant and wild-type constructs
needed_observations: Binding measurements for ZNHIT3 Asp118, Glu148 and Asp85 substitutions and for NUFIP1 Arg475 and His465 substitutions against wild-type partners
Co-immunoprecipitation of the same variants in fibroblasts, with and without CB-839
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Do the predicted interface contacts mediate the measured NUFIP1-ZNHIT3 association and its sensitivity to CB-839?
verification_needs.why_informative: If substitution of the predicted contacts abolishes binding, the modeled interface becomes an experimentally supported interface; if CB-839 sensitivity persists in variants that still bind, the compound is unlikely to act through those contacts.

information_requests: Whether the validation folds used for early stopping and z-scoring in e03 are the same folds whose predictions are reported.

add_nodes.statement: Established: part of the deep model's grouped-CV advantage arises from its evaluation procedure. If the validation folds monitored for early stopping (validation F1-macro, patience 30, up to 150 epochs) are the held-out product-grouped folds on which F1-macro is reported, the stopping epoch is selected on test runs, raising held-out scores independently of release-kinetic information; the classical models were instead tuned in a separate 5-fold inner grid search.

proposed_updates.rationale: Visible Methods details allow test-fold selection; with about 9 runs per fold, epoch selection on held-out F1 can inflate scores.

add_nodes.statement: Candidate (unverified): the deep model's advantage comes from temporal dynamics in the temperature, relative humidity or pressure channels (for example moisture release or heating response differing between products) rather than from gas-resistance VOC release kinetics.

proposed_updates.rationale: Both pipelines take all five channels, and e03 uses full waveforms of every channel, so a shape-based gain need not be VOC-specific.

verification_needs.why_informative: A large drop would attribute part of the gap to selection on test runs; a stable score supports a representation effect.
